output.review_comment: Keep the new p>100 validation and the switch to math.ceil for nearest-rank (please confirm `math` is imported). Don't merge the `p == 50 and n % 2 == 0` branch. By the PR's own account, it exists only so test_median_response_time passes. It contradicts the documented contract that results are always input values and never interpolated. It also makes the function inconsistent: p=50 averages while p=49.999 uses nearest-rank. And the PR rewrites the docstring to fit the hack instead of treating the conflict as a spec question. The test and the docstring disagree, and a person who owns the SRE agreement needs to decide which is right. If the median should interpolate, design and document that deliberately (e.g. a separate median function). If not, fix the test's expected value (120) with sign-off. Please remove the special case and the docstring change, and raise the conflict with the teammate.
